title: Surjectivity and exactness in Mod(O_X) of a ringed space are local lifting of sections (Stacks 01AF, 01AG)
statement: Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space and $\textit{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ the category of sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules on (the open sets of) $X$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; it is abelian, and the kernel of $\varphi:\mathcal G\to\mathcal H$ is the sub-$\mathcal O_X$-module $W\mapsto\ker(\varphi_W)$. Then: (1) a morphism $\varphi:\mathcal G\to\mathcal H$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules is surjective (an epimorphism of $\textit{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$, equivalently $\operatorname{Coker}\varphi=0$) if and only if it is surjective as a map of sheaves: for every open $W\subseteq X$ and every $h\in\mathcal H(W)$ there are an open covering $W=\bigcup_iW_i$ and sections $g_i\in\mathcal G(W_i)$ with $\varphi_{W_i}(g_i)=h|_{W_i}$; (2) a complex $\mathcal F\xrightarrow{\chi}\mathcal G\xrightarrow{\varphi}\mathcal H$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules ($\varphi\circ\chi=0$) is exact at $\mathcal G$ (the image of $\chi$ equals $\operatorname{Ker}\varphi$ in $\textit{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$) if and only if for every open $W\subseteq X$ and every $g\in\mathcal G(W)$ with $\varphi_W(g)=0$ there are an open covering $W=\bigcup_iW_i$ and sections $f_i\in\mathcal F(W_i)$ with $\chi_{W_i}(f_i)=g|_{W_i}$.

source.place: Modules, Section 01AF (label section-kernels: kernels sectionwise, cokernel the sheafified sectionwise cokernel with stalks Coker(phi)_x = Coker(phi_x), lines 102-145) and Lemma 01AG (label lemma-abelian, line 149: Mod(O_X) is abelian and a complex is exact at G iff it is exact on all stalks); with Sheaves, Lemma 0H7H / Definition 007U (sheaves.tex, label lemma-characterize-epi-mono, definition-injective-surjective: surjective on all stalks iff locally surjective), as recorded on lem-weil-pbc-locally-surjective-iff-stalks

proof.text: *Step 1 (epimorphisms are the morphisms with zero cokernel).* $\textit{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ is an abelian category [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], in particular preadditive, and the cokernel of $\varphi:\mathcal G\to\mathcal H$ is $c:\mathcal H\to\operatorname{Coker}\varphi$. By [lem-weil-pbc-preadditive-epi-iff-cokernel-zero], $\varphi$ is an epimorphism if and only if $\operatorname{Coker}\varphi$ is a zero object, i.e. $\operatorname{Coker}\varphi=0$. This is the equivalence of the two descriptions of 'surjective' in (1); it remains to compare them with the local lifting condition (Steps 2 and 3).

source.place: Homology, Lemma 010C (label lemma-characterize-injective), (2): f is surjective (Coker f = 0) iff f is an epimorphism

proof.text: *Step 2 ((1), local lifting implies epimorphism).* Assume that for every open $W$ and $h\in\mathcal H(W)$ there are an open covering $W=\bigcup_iW_i$ and $g_i\in\mathcal G(W_i)$ with $\varphi_{W_i}(g_i)=h|_{W_i}$. Let $\psi_1,\psi_2:\mathcal H\to\mathcal T$ be morphisms of $\mathcal O_X$-modules with $\psi_1\circ\varphi=\psi_2\circ\varphi$, and put $\psi=\psi_1-\psi_2$ (sectionwise difference), so $\psi\circ\varphi=0$. For $W$, $h$, $W_i$, $g_i$ as above, $\psi_W(h)|_{W_i}=\psi_{W_i}(h|_{W_i})=\psi_{W_i}(\varphi_{W_i}(g_i))=0$ for all $i$, since $\psi$ commutes with restrictions; as $\mathcal T$ is a sheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], a section whose restrictions to the members of an open covering vanish is $0$, so $\psi_W(h)=0$. Hence $\psi=0$, i.e. $\psi_1=\psi_2$, and $\varphi$ is an epimorphism.

source.place: Sheaves, Definition 007U (label definition-injective-surjective), (5), and Lemma 0H7H (label lemma-characterize-epi-mono), (2): surjective maps of sheaves are epimorphisms (proof omitted there; written out here)

proof.text: *Step 3 ((1), epimorphism implies local lifting).* Assume $\varphi$ is an epimorphism, so $\operatorname{Coker}\varphi=0$ by Step 1. By the construction of cokernels in $\textit{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], $\operatorname{Coker}\varphi=\mathcal Q^\#$ is the sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] of the presheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules $\mathcal Q:U\mapsto\mathcal H(U)/\varphi_U(\mathcal G(U))$ (restrictions induced by those of $\mathcal H$, which carry $\varphi_U(\mathcal G(U))$ into $\varphi_V(\mathcal G(V))$ as $\varphi$ commutes with restrictions), with $c$ the composite of the quotient maps $\mathcal H(U)\to\mathcal Q(U)$ and of $\theta:\mathcal Q\to\mathcal Q^\#$; and the underlying abelian sheaf of $\mathcal Q^\#$, with $\theta$, is the sheafification of the underlying presheaf of abelian groups of $\mathcal Q$ [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. Let $W\subseteq X$ be open, $h\in\mathcal H(W)$, $x\in W$, and let $q\in\mathcal Q(W)$ be the class of $h$. Then $\theta_W(q)\in\mathcal Q^\#(W)=0$, so its germ $\theta_x(q_x)=(\theta_W(q))_x$ is $0$ (stalks and germs as in [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]). By [lem-weil-pbc-stalk-sheafification-space] $\theta_x:\mathcal Q_x\to\mathcal Q^\#_x$ is an isomorphism, hence $q_x=0=0_x$, and by the description of equality of germs [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] there is an open $V_x$ with $x\in V_x\subseteq W$ and $q|_{V_x}=0$ in $\mathcal Q(V_x)=\mathcal H(V_x)/\varphi_{V_x}(\mathcal G(V_x))$. Since $q|_{V_x}$ is the class of $h|_{V_x}$, there is $g_x\in\mathcal G(V_x)$ with $\varphi_{V_x}(g_x)=h|_{V_x}$. The opens $V_x$, $x\in W$, cover $W$, which is the local lifting condition of (1). (This is the stalk statement $\operatorname{Coker}(\varphi)_x=\operatorname{Coker}(\varphi_x)$ of Modules, Section 01AF, used in the direction needed.) Together with Steps 1 and 2 this proves (1).

source.place: Modules, Section 01AF (label section-kernels): Coker(phi) is the sheafification of U |-> G(U)/phi(F(U)), and Coker(phi)_x = Coker(phi_x) because stalks commute with sheafification (Sheaves, Lemma 007Z, label lemma-stalk-sheafification)

proof.text: *Step 4 ((2), reduction to an epimorphism onto the kernel).* Let $\mathcal F\xrightarrow{\chi}\mathcal G\xrightarrow{\varphi}\mathcal H$ be a complex of $\mathcal O_X$-modules. Its kernel $k:\mathcal K=\operatorname{Ker}\varphi\to\mathcal G$ is the sub-$\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal K(W)=\{g\in\mathcal G(W):\varphi_W(g)=0\}$ with the restrictions of $\mathcal G$ and $k$ the inclusion [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Since $\varphi\circ\chi=0$, $\chi_W(\mathcal F(W))\subseteq\mathcal K(W)$ for every open $W$, so $\chi=k\circ\chi'$ where $\chi'_W:\mathcal F(W)\to\mathcal K(W)$, $f\mapsto\chi_W(f)$; the $\chi'_W$ are $\mathcal O_X(W)$-linear and commute with restrictions (those of $\mathcal K$ being those of $\mathcal G$), so $\chi'$ is a morphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules, and it is the unique one with $k\circ\chi'=\chi$ ($k$ is injective on sections). By [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-exact-iff-epi-kernel-lift] in the abelian category $\textit{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$, the complex is exact at $\mathcal G$ ($\operatorname{Im}\chi=\operatorname{Ker}\varphi$, [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]) if and only if $\chi':\mathcal F\to\mathcal K$ is an epimorphism.

source.place: Homology, Definition 010E (label definition-exact) and Lemma 010C (label lemma-characterize-injective); kernels in Mod(O_X): Modules, Section 01AF (label section-kernels)

proof.text: *Step 5 ((2), conclusion).* Apply (1) (Steps 1-3) to the morphism $\chi':\mathcal F\to\mathcal K$ of Step 4: $\chi'$ is an epimorphism if and only if for every open $W$ and every $g\in\mathcal K(W)$ there are an open covering $W=\bigcup_iW_i$ and $f_i\in\mathcal F(W_i)$ with $\chi'_{W_i}(f_i)=g|_{W_i}$ in $\mathcal K(W_i)$. As $\mathcal K(W)$ consists of the $g\in\mathcal G(W)$ with $\varphi_W(g)=0$, the restrictions of $\mathcal K$ are those of $\mathcal G$, and $\chi'_{W_i}(f_i)=\chi_{W_i}(f_i)$, this is exactly the local lifting condition of (2). With Step 4 this proves (2).

lean.statement: theorem module_exactness_local_lifting (X : RingedSpace.{u}) : (∀ (F G : SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X)) (φ : F ⟶ G) (W : Opens X), Set.range (ConcreteCategory.hom ((kernel.ι φ).val.app (op W))) = {g | φ.val.app (op W) g = 0}) ∧ (∀ (F G : SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X)) (φ : F ⟶ G), (Epi φ ↔ IsZero (cokernel φ)) ∧ ((∀ (W : Opens X) (t : G.val.obj (op W)), (∃ (I : Type u) (V : I → Opens X) (hV : ∀ i, V i ≤ W) (g : ∀ i, F.val.obj (op (V i))), (⨆ i, V i) = W ∧ ∀ i, φ.val.app (op (V i)) (g i) = G.val.map (homOfLE (hV i)).op t)) ↔ Epi φ)) ∧ (∀ (F G H : SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X)) (χ : F ⟶ G) (φ : G ⟶ H) (h : χ ≫ φ = 0), (ShortComplex.mk χ φ h).Exact ↔ ∀ (W : Opens X) (g : G.val.obj (op W)), φ.val.app (op W) g = 0 → ∃ (I : Type u) (V : I → Opens X) (hV : ∀ i, V i ≤ W) (f : ∀ i, F.val.obj (op (V i))), (⨆ i, V i) = W ∧ ∀ i, χ.val.app (op (V i)) (f i) = G.val.map (homOfLE (hV i)).op g)
